input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
input.rationale: The IP provisions meet our preferred position. Section 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and pre-existing/independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right (reinforced by 15.1's bar on selling Customer Data or training models on it). Section 14.2 vests Deliverables in Customer on creation with a present assignment from Vendor and personnel assignments. Section 14.3 lets Vendor retain only Vendor Technology while back-licensing anything embedded in a Deliverable through the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence in Section 13.2 (which includes modify and derivative-work rights). Section 14.4 excludes joint ownership absent a signed instrument and keeps feedback rights with Customer. No assignment of Customer IP or data to Vendor and no vendor-owned deliverables without licence-back, so nothing to redline; the payment condition in 14.2 and the telemetry carve-out in the Customer Data definition (1.3) are ordinary and noted only for awareness.
